description: Estimates of domestic tax evasion in Switzerland from 1932 to 2009 as compiled by Stefan Howald (December 2010, published by Erklärung von Bern / Public Eye): the 1940 Wehropfer evaluation of the federal tax administration (1944), the federal council report on the motion Eggenberger (1962) with the first withholding-tax extrapolation, the income tax evasion rates of Weck-Hannemann/Pommerehne and Feld/Frey (1965 to 1995), tax morale survey ranks (ISSP, WVS), shadow economy shares (Schneider, seco), the political estimates of Strahm (2003) and Badertscher (2010), and Howald's own withholding-tax extrapolation for 2008 and 2009 with the tax rates proposed by Olivier Longchamp. Every number of the paper is a value with its original source; the extrapolation chains are formulas with calc-validation. Where a recomputation differs from the rounded number printed in the paper, the printed number is kept as the value and the exact recomputation carries the word calculated, with the difference stated in the description. Only the two withholding tax rates of 1958 and 1960 (25 % and 27 %) are not in the paper; they come from the ESTV history of the withholding tax and reproduce the paper's figures. Parameters that the sources set by judgement (yields, tax rates, the unclaimed share of foreigners) carry the word assumed with a confidence; a value read off a bar chart carries assumed as well.

words.name: bond

words.name: deposit

words.name: gold

words.name: undeclared

words.name: exempt

words.name: liable
words.description: subject to the tax in question.

words.name: partnership

words.name: unclaimed

words.name: foreigner

words.name: yield
words.description: the income return on an investment as a ratio of its value.

words.name: lost
words.description: of a tax: not collected because the tax base was hidden.

words.name: shadow
words.description: of an economy: hidden from the state.

words.name: GNP

words.name: morale
words.description: the willingness of a group to comply with a norm; here the intrinsic motivation to pay taxes.

words.name: justified
words.description: of an action: held to be acceptable; a survey answer category.

words.name: never
words.description: at no time; the lowest category of a justifiability scale.

words.name: bribe
words.description: money given to a person in a position of trust to influence their behaviour.

words.name: marginal
words.description: of a tax rate: the rate on the last unit of income.

words.name: taxable
words.description: subject to tax after the deductions of the tax law.

words.name: Wehropfer
words.description: the one-off Swiss federal levy on wealth of 1940 (first Wehropfer) raised to cover the extraordinary armament and war economy expenditure; the 1944 study of the federal tax administration compared its declarations with the statistical stock of securities and savings.

words.name: ISSP
words.description: International Social Survey Programme, a cross-national collaboration on social science surveys.

words.name: WVS
words.description: World Values Survey, a global research project exploring people's values and beliefs.

words.name: Schwyz

triples.name: 2005 to 2007
triples.description: the fifth wave of the World Values Survey, fielded from 2005 to 2007.

triples.name: canton and municipality
triples.description: the cantonal and the municipal level of the Swiss state taken together, as the tax statistics report them.

triples.name: tax evasion
triples.description: an illegal attempt to lessen the payment of taxes by individuals, corporations or trusts; in Swiss law an administrative offence distinct from tax fraud.

triples.name: tax evasion rate
triples.description: the evaded part of the tax base as a ratio of the true tax base; with the phrase withholding tax the ratio of the unclaimed to the total withholding tax of residents.

triples.name: tax rate
triples.description: the ratio at which a tax base is taxed.

triples.name: marginal tax rate
triples.description: the tax rate on the last unit of income.

triples.name: income tax
triples.description: a tax imposed on individuals or entities in respect of the income or profits earned by them.

triples.name: wealth tax
triples.description: a tax on an entity's holdings of assets; in Switzerland levied by the cantons and municipalities only.

triples.name: income and wealth tax
triples.description: the income tax and the wealth tax of the cantons and municipalities taken together.

triples.name: income tax evasion rate
triples.description: the difference between the household income reported to the cantonal tax authority and the independently measured household income, as a ratio of gross household income (Weck-Hannemann and Pommerehne 1989, p. 524).

triples.name: withholding tax
triples.description: the Swiss Verrechnungssteuer, a federal tax deducted at source from capital income since 1944 and refunded to recipients who declare the income, so that the unclaimed part indicates undeclared capital income.

triples.name: withholding tax rate
triples.description: the legal rate of the Swiss withholding tax on capital income: 25 % from 1945, 27 % from 1959, 30 % from 1967 and 35 % from 1976.

triples.name: withholding tax revenue
triples.description: the gross receipts of the withholding tax before refunds (row A of Howald's table).

triples.name: reclaimed withholding tax
triples.description: the withholding tax refunded to the taxpayers who declared the income.

triples.name: unclaimed withholding tax
triples.description: the withholding tax that was never reclaimed (row B of Howald's table).

triples.name: reclaimed withholding tax of residents
triples.description: row E of Howald's table: refunds to Swiss residents.

triples.name: reclaimed withholding tax of foreigners
triples.description: row C of Howald's table: refunds to foreign applicants under double taxation treaties.

triples.name: unclaimed withholding tax of residents
triples.description: row F of Howald's table: the unclaimed withholding tax attributed to Swiss residents, B minus D.

triples.name: unclaimed withholding tax of foreigners
triples.description: row D of Howald's table: the part of the unclaimed withholding tax attributed to foreign owners.

triples.name: unclaimed share
triples.description: the unclaimed part of a withholding tax as a ratio of the total.

triples.name: unclaimed share of foreigners
triples.description: the ratio of the withholding tax that foreign owners fail to reclaim to the withholding tax they do reclaim; Howald sets it to 25 %.

triples.name: foreigner share
triples.description: the part of a withholding tax amount that belongs to foreign owners.

triples.name: capital income
triples.description: interest and dividends; the income the Swiss withholding tax is levied on.

triples.name: undeclared capital income
triples.description: the capital income implied by the unclaimed withholding tax of residents, divided by the withholding tax rate.

triples.name: undeclared wealth
triples.description: the wealth implied by the undeclared capital income at an average yield.

triples.name: undeclared share
triples.description: the undeclared part of a tax base as a ratio of the whole.

triples.name: average yield
triples.description: the average return on capital used to capitalise undeclared capital income into undeclared wealth.

triples.name: lost tax
triples.description: the tax revenue not collected because of tax evasion.

triples.name: federal lost tax
triples.description: the tax revenue lost by the Swiss Confederation.

triples.name: cantonal and municipal lost tax
triples.description: the tax revenue lost by the cantons and municipalities together.

triples.name: target holdings
triples.description: the Sollbestand of the 1944 study: the stock of securities at market value from the statistical yearbook and of savings deposits from the banking statistics, less Swiss securities in foreign hands, plus foreign securities in Swiss hands.

triples.name: declared holdings
triples.description: the holdings declared for the Wehropfer.

triples.name: undeclared holdings
triples.description: the holdings that remained untaxed by the Wehropfer: target holdings less declared and exempt holdings.

triples.name: exempt holdings
triples.description: the holdings of owners not liable to the Wehropfer.

triples.name: liable holdings
triples.description: the target holdings less the exempt holdings; the base Munz used for his 30 % evasion rate.

triples.name: undeclared share of target holdings
triples.description: the undeclared holdings as a ratio of the target holdings; the rate of the 1944 study.

triples.name: undeclared share of liable holdings
triples.description: the undeclared holdings as a ratio of the liable holdings; the rate of Munz (1944).

triples.name: natural and legal person
triples.description: the row of the 1944 table that joins natural and legal persons.

triples.name: savings deposit
triples.description: the Sparguthaben of the Swiss banking statistics.

triples.name: domestic security
triples.description: a security issued in Switzerland, subject to the withholding tax.

triples.name: foreign security
triples.description: a security issued abroad, free of the Swiss withholding tax.

triples.name: banknote and gold
triples.description: cash and gold holdings, the category the 1962 report estimated together.

triples.name: shadow economy
triples.description: the part of an economy that is neither taxed nor monitored by the government.

triples.name: national income
triples.description: the total income of the residents of a country in a year.

triples.name: tax morale
triples.description: the intrinsic motivation to pay taxes, measured by surveys that ask whether cheating on taxes can be justified.

triples.name: never justified
triples.description: the survey answer that the behaviour asked about can never be justified; the share of respondents choosing it.

triples.name: country count
triples.description: the number of countries in a survey ranking.

formulas.name: unclaimed foreign withholding tax (formula)
formulas.description: row D of Howald's table: the withholding tax that foreign owners presumably failed to reclaim, as a share of what they did reclaim
formulas.expression: "unclaimed withholding tax of foreigners" = "reclaimed withholding tax of foreigners" * "unclaimed share of foreigners"

formulas.name: unclaimed resident withholding tax (formula)
formulas.description: row F = B - D of Howald's table: the unclaimed withholding tax attributed to Swiss residents
formulas.expression: "unclaimed withholding tax of residents" = "unclaimed withholding tax" - "unclaimed withholding tax of foreigners"

formulas.name: unclaimed share (formula)
formulas.description: the unclaimed withholding tax as a ratio of the gross withholding tax revenue (column % of row B)

formulas.name: withholding tax evasion rate (formula)
formulas.description: Howald's evasion rate: F divided by E + F, the unclaimed withholding tax of residents as a ratio of all withholding tax of residents
formulas.expression: "tax evasion rate" = "unclaimed withholding tax of residents" / ( "reclaimed withholding tax of residents" + "unclaimed withholding tax of residents" )

formulas.name: undeclared capital income (formula)
formulas.description: the capital income on which the unclaimed withholding tax of residents was withheld, so the income that was not declared; used by the 1962 report and by Howald
formulas.expression: "undeclared capital income" = "unclaimed withholding tax of residents" / "withholding tax rate"

formulas.name: undeclared wealth (formula)
formulas.description: the wealth that yields the undeclared capital income at the average yield

formulas.name: lost income tax (formula)
formulas.description: the income tax lost on the undeclared capital income at the average income tax rate
formulas.expression: "lost income tax" = "undeclared capital income" * "average income tax rate"

formulas.name: lost wealth tax (formula)
formulas.description: the wealth tax lost on the undeclared wealth at the average wealth tax rate
formulas.expression: "lost wealth tax" = "undeclared wealth" * "average wealth tax rate"

formulas.name: lost tax (formula)
formulas.description: the lost income tax and the lost wealth tax together

formulas.name: foreigner share of refunds (formula)
formulas.description: the refunds to foreign applicants as a ratio of all refunds (footnote 20 of Howald)
formulas.expression: "foreigner share" = "reclaimed withholding tax of foreigners" / ( "reclaimed withholding tax of foreigners" + "reclaimed withholding tax of residents" )

formulas.name: undeclared share of target holdings (formula)
formulas.description: the rate of the 1944 study: undeclared holdings as a ratio of the target holdings
formulas.expression: "undeclared share of target holdings" = "undeclared holdings" / "target holdings"

formulas.name: exempt holdings (formula)
formulas.description: the exempt holdings of natural and legal persons together

formulas.name: liable holdings (formula)
formulas.description: the target holdings less the exempt holdings, the base of Munz (1944)

formulas.name: undeclared share of liable holdings (formula)
formulas.description: the rate of Munz (1944): undeclared holdings as a ratio of the liable holdings
formulas.expression: "undeclared share of liable holdings" = "undeclared holdings" / "liable holdings"
